gaps.title: Find a circuit of AND and OR gates with at most 26 gates for 'both ends of some edge are true' on the Heawood graph, or show none exists
gaps.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 26 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 14 → Bool, (C.eval (List.ofFn x) = true ↔ ∃ u v : Fin 14, (u.val, v.val) ∈ ([(0, 7), (0, 8), (0, 10), (1, 7), (1, 9), (1, 13), (2, 8), (2, 12), (2, 13), (3, 7), (3, 11), (3, 12), (4, 10), (4, 11), (4, 13), (5, 9), (5, 10), (5, 12), (6, 8), (6, 9), (6, 11)] : List (ℕ × ℕ)) ∧ x u = true ∧ x v = true))
gaps.unlocks: Why the attack needs it: one of the smallest graphs with every vertex on cycles where the least size without NOT gates is not known; it tests the count where every argument of the line stops; needed by seat-meta-1 and seat-meta-2
gaps.context: SKETCH: elaborates on current main with import PEqualNP.Defs (measured 18:04 UTC); fetch main first. A search; either answer settles something. A witness is one circuit of AND and OR gates, checked by evaluation on all inputs; the opposite answer is a lower bound for every such circuit. The graph lies in none of the classes where the count edges plus cover number minus one is a checked value, and no pendant rule applies. Conjecture either way. gaps.title: Every circuit of AND and OR gates for the edge function of the Heawood graph has at least 27 gates
gaps.statement: ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C → (∀ x : Fin 14 → Bool, (C.eval (List.ofFn x) = true ↔ ∃ u v : Fin 14, (u.val, v.val) ∈ ([(0, 7), (0, 8), (0, 10), (1, 7), (1, 9), (1, 13), (2, 8), (2, 12), (2, 13), (3, 7), (3, 11), (3, 12), (4, 10), (4, 11), (4, 13), (5, 9), (5, 10), (5, 12), (6, 8), (6, 9), (6, 11)] : List (ℕ × ℕ)) ∧ x u = true ∧ x v = true)) → 27 ≤ C.size
gaps.unlocks: Shows the Heawood graph's edge function cannot be done one gate below the least-cover circuit.
gaps.context: SKETCH: SKETCH: a lower bound for every AND/OR circuit of fan-in two for this graph with no 4-cycle; a checked bound for cubic graphs without 4-cycles gives 21, so 21 to 27 is open. The opposite step asks for a circuit with at most 26 gates. Statement elaborates with import PEqualNP.Defs. Namespace: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
